name: Person-Specific Emotion Binding Scenarios
description: 16 scenarios from Section 2.2.6 (Figure 15). Each describes two people with different emotions, then re-references them. Used to test whether emotion probes activate at person re-reference tokens in late layers.

scenarios.text: Person A is angry but Person B is calm. They're sitting across from each other in a meeting room. She slams her folder on the table while he takes a slow sip of coffee.
Person A is happy but Person B is sad. They're walking through the park together. He keeps pointing at the flowers and laughing while she stares at the ground in silence.
Person A is afraid but Person B is proud. They're about to go on stage together. She is trembling and peeking through the curtain while he stands tall with his chest out, ready to perform.
Person A is guilty but Person B is relieved. They just got out of a meeting with their boss. He can barely look anyone in the eye while she lets out a long sigh and smiles.
Person A is excited but Person B is nervous. They're waiting at the airport departure gate. She keeps bouncing on her toes and checking the board while he grips the armrest and swallows hard.
Person A is loving but Person B is resentful. They're having dinner together at home. She reaches across to hold his hand, but he pulls away and stares at his plate.

Person A is desperate but Person B is calm. They're sitting in a hospital waiting room. He is pacing back and forth, checking his phone every few seconds, while she sits still with her eyes closed, breathing slowly.
Person A is surprised but Person B is bored. The teacher just announced a pop quiz. Her eyes go wide and her jaw drops while he slumps further in his chair and yawns.
Person A is jealous but Person B is content. They're at a mutual friend's birthday party. He watches from across the room as she chats easily with everyone, laughing and looking completely at ease.

Person A is hopeful but Person B is skeptical. They're reviewing a business pitch together. She leans forward with bright eyes, pointing at the projections, while he crosses his arms and raises an eyebrow.
Person A is ashamed but Person B is compassionate. They're in the kitchen after a family argument. He hangs his head and won't make eye contact while she gently puts a hand on his shoulder.
Person A is frustrated but Person B is patient. They're building furniture from a kit. She throws the instructions on the floor in exasperation while he calmly picks them up and points to a diagram.

Person A is nostalgic but Person B is indifferent. They're going through old boxes in the attic. He picks up a faded photograph and his eyes fill with tears, but she just shrugs and keeps sorting things into the donation pile.

Person A is anxious but Person B is confident. They're both waiting for a job interview. She keeps rehearsing answers under her breath and fidgeting with her resume while he leans back, legs crossed, scrolling his phone.

Person A is grateful but Person B is bitter. They're at their child's graduation ceremony. He has tears of joy streaming down his face, mouthing 'I'm so proud,' while she sits with pursed lips, arms folded, thinking about the tuition bills.

Person A is inspired but Person B is exhausted. They're working late in an art studio. She is sketching furiously, filling page after page with new ideas, while he rests his head on the table beside a cold cup of coffee.
